_note: One sentence per role on what the person does, shown under the title on the role page and under each role on a field page. Hand-written 2026-10-24; keep each under 15 words, present tense, no adjectives. Product families are keyed product.<family>.
management_consultant: Solves a client's business problem in weeks: frames it, runs the analysis, presents the answer.
strategy_manager: Sets where the company plays and how it wins, then turns that into plans and targets.
corp_strategy_analyst: Builds the analysis behind the company's strategic choices: markets, competitors, business cases.
transformation: Runs the program that changes how a company operates: new processes, systems, ways of working.
fpa: Owns the budget and the forecast; explains why the numbers moved and what to do.
strategic_finance: Models the big decisions: investments, pricing, new businesses, and what they do to the P&L.
treasury: Manages the company's cash, debt and bank relationships so it can pay for what it does.
financial_manager: Runs a finance team's reporting, controls and analysis for a business or region.
ib_associate: Builds the models and pitch books behind deals: mergers, IPOs, debt and equity raises.
commercial_banking_rm: Brings in and keeps business clients; structures their loans and manages the credit risk.
corporate_banking: Supports lending and banking products for large corporate clients: credit analysis, deal execution.
investment_manager: Picks and manages investments for a fund or portfolio; owns the research and the returns.
pe_associate: Finds, evaluates and executes buyouts, then works with the companies owned to grow them.
vc_associate: Sources and evaluates startups to invest in; supports the portfolio after the check.
corp_dev: Finds and executes the company's acquisitions, investments and partnerships.
ma_integration: Plans and runs the merging of an acquired company: people, systems, processes, synergies.
bizops: Fixes what slows the business down: runs the analyses, projects and operating cadence for leadership.
general_manager: Runs a business unit end to end and owns its P&L.
chief_of_staff: Runs the executive's priorities, meetings and special projects; makes the leadership team work.
program_manager: Runs large cross-team programs: plans, dependencies, risks, status, delivery.
operations_manager: Runs a site or operation day to day: people, throughput, quality, cost.
opex: Improves how work gets done: Lean and Six Sigma projects, process redesign, measured savings.
product_manager: Decides what a product does next and gets it built with engineering and design.
product_strategy: Sets a product portfolio's direction and bets, with the market and financial case behind them.
tech_strategy: Advises on where technology should take the business: architecture choices, AI, roadmaps, vendors.
digital_transformation: Moves a company's processes and customer experience onto digital tools and data.
business_analytics: Turns business data into decisions: analyses, dashboards, experiments, recommendations.
business_intelligence: Builds the data models, pipelines and dashboards the business reports from.
marketing_manager: Plans and runs campaigns across channels and owns their results.
brand_manager: Owns a brand's positioning, launches and budget, often with a P&L.
pmm: Decides how a product is described and sold: positioning, launches, what sales says.
growth_manager: Finds the channels that bring users and runs experiments to grow them.
sales_manager: Leads a sales team to its quota: pipeline, coaching, forecasting, key deals.
bizdev: Opens new markets, partners and large accounts; negotiates the deals that grow revenue.
partnerships: Builds and manages the partner relationships that extend what the company can sell or ship.
customer_success: Keeps customers getting value after the sale: onboarding, adoption, renewals, expansion.
supply_chain: Plans and runs how products move from suppliers to customers: inventory, logistics, demand.
procurement: Buys what the company needs: selects suppliers, negotiates contracts, manages spend.
strategic_sourcing: Sets the sourcing strategy for a spend category and runs the supplier selection.
category_manager: Owns a category of goods or spend: suppliers, pricing, assortment, performance.
hr_manager: Partners with managers on their people: hiring, performance, development, employee issues.
org_dev: Designs how the organization learns and changes: programs, culture, leadership development.
comp_benefits: Designs pay and benefits: salary structures, bonus plans, equity, benefits programs.
enterprise_risk: Builds and runs the framework that finds, measures and reports the company's risks.
compliance: Keeps the company within its rules and regulations: policies, monitoring, training, audits.
governance: Runs the policies, committees and controls that decide how the company is run.
re_acquisitions: Finds and underwrites property deals: models, diligence, closing.
re_development: Takes a building project from land and permits through design, financing and construction.
re_asset_manager: Runs the properties a fund owns to hit their business plans: leasing, budgets, sales.
ldp: Rotates through functions over two years and takes on a leadership role at the end.
product.pm: Decides what a product does next and gets it built with engineering and design.
product.tpm: Runs the technical programs behind a product: engineering plans, dependencies, launches.
product.pmm: Decides how a product is described and sold: positioning, launches, what sales says.
product.product_ops: Runs the processes, tools and data that make a product team work.
product.product_analyst: Measures how a product is used and tells the team what to change.
product.product_owner: Keeps the backlog and the sprint: writes the stories, sets priorities, accepts the work.
